research.summary: Discovery is a fail-closed, network-independent core: /json/ archive inventory and projects.json retain separate semantics; only active datasets.toml JSON archives are tracked; uncertain HTTP observations require download; exact downloaded bytes are ZIP-validated and SHA-256 identified; extraction and live transport remain outside PH2.

design.boundary: Pure inventory/HEAD/retry/download-verification/content-state functions only; no live HTTP adapter, no archive extraction, no workflow/CLI ownership.
design.decision_rule: Only a syntactically valid strong ETag plus matching Content-Length may authorize unchanged without downloading. Weak, missing, malformed, or changed validators require byte verification.

behavior.tracked_scope: Active JSON archive inputs from datasets.toml; shared inputs are polled once; TEI remains a separate upstream.
behavior.fail_closed: 5xx is retryable unavailable; unresolved redirects/client errors are protocol failures; missing/weak/malformed validators require download; soft-404 and non-ZIP bodies are rejected; HEAD/GET byte-length disagreement is rejected; archive links cannot escape the configured listing origin/directory.
behavior.content_identity: SHA-256 over exact downloaded bytes; byte-identical republication refreshes metadata without rebuild; changed SHA requires rebuild; equivalent SHA hexadecimal case is canonicalized rather than treated as a content change.

completion_blocker.reason: PH2's independent discovery semantics are implemented and tested, but live integration must consume the PH1 upstream configuration/lock and authenticated normal-TLS transport before PH2 can be finalized.

resume_gate: When P-002.PH1 is done, integrate the real transport/configuration without weakening TLS or PH2 fail-closed rules, run real upstream observations, refresh this evidence with the integration run, and perform a fresh exact-head adversarial review before merge.
